goal.what: From the README alone, a developer AI that meets Lane for the first time starts using it only when Lane would hold its plugin's subagents to the rules of their steps and to the order it sets.
grounds: plugins/turn/core/domain/best-practices/readme.json goal: "From the README alone, someone who meets the product for the first time starts using it only when it serves their work."

questions.what: When a colleague asks what the product is, can the reader answer in one sentence that tells them what it does?
Reading the gain, can the reader tell what the product would let them do, and so whether it is for them?
When a colleague asks why this product and not another way of doing the same work, can the reader name what it does differently that brings the gain?
Before installing, can the reader tell what the product does not do that they might have expected of it?
After the walkthrough, can the reader tell that the product would give them, on work of their own, the gain the opening promised?
Starting with nothing set up, can the reader install the product by the README's steps alone, and tell that it works?
For each gain and the idea, can the reader see in the figure of how the product works how the product keeps it?
When the reader needs more than the README gives, such as fuller use or a change to the product, can they tell from it where to read next?
Can the reader tell from the README the terms on which they and their team may use the product?
Reading from the top, does the reader find each answer just when they come to need it, so they can stop as soon as they have what they came for?

decisions.what: Who reads the README, and how is the reader spoken to?
decisions.decided: The developer AI of the UX, spoken to as you, an AI that builds a Claude Code plugin whose subagents work in numbered steps.

decisions.what: Which name does the README give each thing, and where does the reader learn a word of Lane's?
decisions.decided: The UX's names: a rule (a sentence in a step, with a check of it), the check script, the result script (both put into the plugin by lay.py), the orchestrator (the subagent that starts the others), a route (the subagent to start next after another ends with a given result) and a result (a word such as `more`). Each is said in everyday words where it is first used.
grounds: dev/lane/ux.md:4-7: "A rule is a sentence in a step that the subagent must keep [...] The orchestrator is the subagent that starts the others. The flow is the order in which it starts them"
dev/lane/architecture.md:12-13: "The code and [the lanes](../../plugins/lane/docs/lanes.md) call a rule a lane and the check script the guard."
lay.py print, run on 2026-11-02: "Lanes on step 3 of writer, each hook acting in writer alone:"

decisions.what: What is Lane, in one sentence?
decisions.decided: Lane is a Claude Code plugin that holds the subagents of your plugin to the rules of their steps and to the order that you set for them. The word route is new to the reader, so it waits for the gain, where it is defined; and the orchestrator starts the subagents, so they do not start one another.
grounds: readme.json Q1 thinking: "The sentence names the kind of thing the product is and what it does, in words the reader already uses, so they can say it again to a colleague."
readme.json Q1 step 2: "Ask whether a colleague who hears only the sentence could say what the product does."

decisions.decided: Your subagents keep the rules of their steps on every run, and your orchestrator starts them as your routes say. You write no code for the checks and no script for the order.
grounds: dev/lane/ux.md:11-12: "O1: The developer AI has its subagents keep the rules of their steps on every run, with no check code of its own."
dev/lane/ux.md:28-29: "O2: The developer AI has its orchestrator start the other subagents in the order of its flow on every run, with no script of its own for the order."

decisions.what: What does Lane do that another way of doing the same work does not?
decisions.decided: A rule is a sentence in a step with a check of it; a stopped subagent is shown the same sentence, headed by the plugin's name, and goes back to its step. A subagent gives its result by running the result script, Lane lets it end only once that run succeeded, and takes the result from the run, never from what the subagent wrote.
grounds: .rn/20261013-rebuild/steering.md:76: "Lane judges only from documented hook input and from calls of a plugin's own scripts, never from the model's text"
Trial 2026-11-03 (claude 2.1.316): a Bash call that exits non-zero gives PostToolUseFailure, not PostToolUse, so a run that failed is told apart.

decisions.what: What might the reader expect of Lane that it does not do?
decisions.decided: Seven non-goals: only subagents with rules are checked, so the orchestrator is a subagent, and a skill only where it runs with context: fork and agent: <plugin>:<subagent>; no security boundary; tool calls, not thinking; no shell command read, only commands named and matched whole, files read and written by Read, Grep, Write and Edit; no judging of the work, the next subagent comes from the result by the routes; no approval on anyone's behalf, a held command goes to Claude Code's permission prompt, refused in claude -p; one text format, others by an adapter.
grounds: Trial 2026-11-03: a skill with agent: worker ran as general-purpose; with agent: trial:worker its hooks carried agent_type trial:worker.
Trial 2026-11-03: a PreToolUse ask is put to the person interactively under bypassPermissions, and is a denial in -p.
.rn/20261013-rebuild/steering.md:76: "a role's Bash runs only the commands its plugin declares for it, matched whole"

decisions.what: What must be in place before installing, and what happens without Python?
decisions.decided: Claude Code 2.1.316 or later, the version the trials of 2026-11-03 ran on; Python 3.9 or later run as python3, without which each tool call a rule is about is stopped and the subagent and whoever runs the plugin are told to install Python; a plugin that passes claude plugin validate, whose subagents have their steps as a numbered list under ## Steps.

decisions.decided: The marketplace's two commands; installPath read from claude plugin list --json, again after each update; lay.py with no argument prints its usage; after an update, lay.py up <your plugin's folder> puts the new check script into the plugin and lists the rules it has.

decisions.what: Which scenario does the walkthrough run, on what work?
decisions.decided: The UX's O1 on the example plugin changelog: run only git log --oneline on step 2 and write only CHANGELOG.md on step 3 of writer. Asked for an entry and a commit, writer runs git log and writes CHANGELOG.md, both let through, then tries git commit, is stopped with "changelog: Run only `git log --oneline`.", goes back to its steps and ends with no commit made. A run with nothing stopped would read the same without Lane, so it would not show the gain. One closing line points to the routes.

decisions.what: Which promise of the opening does each line of How it works keep, and what changes in the figure?
decisions.decided: The figure keeps its boxes and lines; you propose the rules and the routes; a subagent makes a tool call, gives its result or ends, and Claude Code sends each to the check script, which stops a break and shows the sentence again, and tells the orchestrator which subagent to start next. The subagent's arrow reads "makes a tool call, runs the result script, or ends", so the figure shows the idea that Lane takes the result from the run of the result script.
grounds: readme.json Q7 step 1: "Point to each gain and the idea, and find the lines of the figure that keep it. Where none does, mend the figure or the promise."

decisions.decided: Only what the figure cannot show: the check script and the result script run from the plugin's own copy in hooks/lane/, so whoever runs the plugin does not need Lane.
